samples.question: The panel labeled KEY at the top of this image is a 4x4 grid of sixteen cells in which exactly four cells are filled dark gray; the other twelve are blank. Below it are three more 4x4 grids, labeled A, B and C from left to right, whose cells are painted red, blue, green or orange. A cell of the KEY card corresponds to the cell in the same row and the same column of a colour grid, counting rows from the top and columns from the left. The grids are drawn at a different cell size and in a different place than the KEY card, so this row-and-column correspondence is the only alignment that matters and pixel positions never line up. Every colour grid paints each of the four colours in exactly four of its cells, so no colour is rarer or more common than another. In exactly one of the three colour grids, all four cells that the KEY card marks carry one and the same colour; in the other two grids the four marked positions carry at least two different colours. What is that single colour? Answer red, blue, green, or orange.
